note: Seed catalog. Every row is a claimed failure mode with a detection recipe; none has been swept against a live site yet. A row graduates to evidenceStatus 'measured' only after a sweep reproduces it on a live install, verifies the detection recipe catches it, and records the result. SKIPPED and INCONCLUSIVE sweeps are never folded into pass rates.

failureModes.title: config:import exits 0 but the site serves the old config
failureModes.symptom: drush config:import or config:set reports success; a page or form still behaves per the previous configuration.
failureModes.rootCause: Config consumers cache parsed values outside the config factory, or the import did not invalidate the cache tags the affected output depends on.
failureModes.detection: After any config write, read back with get_site_config (state), then probe an affected URL with verify_page. A match on config:get alone is not evidence of delivery.
failureModes.citation: mosaic-headless 'never trust the commit' pattern, adapted

failureModes.title: hook_update_N returns early and reports success
failureModes.symptom: The update hook shows as applied; the intended data change did not happen.
failureModes.rootCause: Early-return paths (dependency guards, conditional skips) return without doing work; drush updb reports success either way.
failureModes.detection: After updb, assert the intended data state via state-plane reads (entity counts, field values), never via the update log.

failureModes.title: Custom plugin class parses cleanly but is never discovered
failureModes.symptom: No error anywhere; the plugin's behavior is simply absent.
failureModes.rootCause: Wrong namespace/file location relative to the module's src/ tree, or missing/incorrect Drupal attribute — discovery is convention-driven, not loader-driven.
failureModes.detection: Consult the knowledge plane (discovery docs) before writing; probe the discovered plugin list via the state plane after. Both, not either.

failureModes.title: Wrong service/interface injection fatals only on the page that uses it
failureModes.symptom: Site builds and most pages work; one route returns the critical-error screen.
failureModes.rootCause: Autowiring and interface mismatches resolve only at first instantiation on the affected route.
failureModes.detection: verify_page every route the change touches; a 5xx or the critical-error marker is a dead page even when the commit reported success.

failureModes.title: Right content, wrong freshness, no error ever
failureModes.symptom: Updated content does not appear on lists or views that cache by tag.
failureModes.rootCause: The render array lacks the entity's cache tag (or a required cache context), so invalidation never reaches it.
failureModes.detection: After content writes, verify_page the listing URL and compare a marker string; absence with correct backend state implicates cache metadata.

failureModes.title: The page is dead but the HTTP status does not say so
failureModes.symptom: Public page returns a very small body or an error screen under a 200/3xx, or a 5xx with a large HTML wrapper.
failureModes.rootCause: Drupal's critical-error handling and proxy layers can produce non-5xx responses for dead pages.
failureModes.detection: verify_page treats 5xx as dead, matches the critical-error marker, and flags 200s under 64 bytes as suspicious_short.
failureModes.citation: mosaic-headless: 'WordPress's critical error screen is 2,697 bytes and larger than any naive healthy-page floor'
